notes: OUTSIDE: the 30-account iPhone run (memory resident MB) needs the iOS 26.5 simulator runtime, and the push p95 cell needs a real iPhone 17 Pro (the simulator's relay leg is a stand-in); proofs 3 and 4 (lead). Open for the owner: confirm PUSH_ARRIVAL_P95_S = 180 s (docs/CONSTANTS.md:62). Built here: --selftest in perf/memory-iphone.py (proof 1) and perf/push-arrival.py (proof 2): each runs the script's own main() against a stand-in socket and compares exit code and verdict with the expected pair of each case: memory at the limit (250) exit 0, 0.5 MB over exit 1, the fixture at 29 accounts exit 1 NOT JUDGED, no measure, a busy machine, no socket; push p95 at the limit exit 0, one ms over exit 1, two slow pushes in twenty exit 1 while their mean is far below the limit, no measure, a busy machine, no socket; the push cases also count 20 pushes delivered. Each of the six script mutants is a one-line edit of a judge (>= for >, the account check off, the load gate off, the mean for the p95). CHANGED BEHAVIOUR in both scripts: the load gate compared the load per core with PERF_LOAD_MAX = 12, which the ledger states as the one-minute load average (docs/CONSTANTS.md:43), so the gate could not trip; it now compares the one-minute load average (new function load_avg()) and the case busy-machine proves it. The old text of this note on PERF_LOAD_MAX being missing is out of date (the row exists). Proof indices: 0 constants, 1 memory selftest, 2 push selftest, 3 lead memory, 4 lead push. The earlier mutants on proof 0 are unchanged. Claims: (a) memory-iphone exits 1 above 250 MB on the 30-account fixture: perf/memory-iphone.py:23-36 constant(), :88-104 main (accounts/count must equal the fixture's 30 else NOT JUDGED), limit constants.rs:12 and docs/CONSTANTS.md:16; (b) push-arrival exits 1 above PUSH_ARRIVAL_P95_S: perf/push-arrival.py:105-125, N = 20 pushes (:91), p95 :99-101, constants.rs:60 and docs/CONSTANTS.md:62. Proof 0 reads the constants through the scripts' own parser (no app, no socket, nothing compiled); it does not prove the exit code. Both scripts print the line `1 checks, F failed, U not judged` and exit 1 unless WITHIN BUDGET (:70-83), and print their verdict to stderr; so proofs 1 and 2 must read both streams. The mutants are the value-rows the scripts read: breaking either makes proof 0 print another number. I did not run any of these. Standing rule applies: both scripts read the machine load and the app's memory, they do not themselves add any load. | Round 2 (iphone-rig, 2026-11-12): the iOS 26.5 runtime is installed and scripts/iphone-rig.sh runs the phone with no window (docs/lanes/iphone-rig.md); the lead proofs below are the exact commands through it. IPHONE_APP and MAC_APP are the built .app bundles (the Mac one is the one launch-one.sh takes). Proof 3 now runs through the rig on a calm machine (PERF_LOAD_MAX 12). What stays outside: proof 4 only, the push p95 cell, which needs a real iPhone 17 Pro (the simulator's relay leg is a stand-in), and the owner's confirmation of PUSH_ARRIVAL_P95_S = 180 s (docs/CONSTANTS.md:62). | Round 6: perf/memory-iphone.py compares the load per core (PERF_LOAD_MAX x cores / 12, the ledger: one runnable per core on a 12-core Mac), names both figures when it does not judge, and has a broken copy memory/load-raw (selftest 9 cases).
